# 2 Samuel Chapter 9 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 177v–178r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_009_page_001.jpg, 2SA_009_page_002.jpg

---

**9:1** And-said David, "Is-there yet [anyone]-who remains to-[the]-house of-Sha'ul, and-I-will-do with-him covenant-faithfulness [chesed] for-the-sake-of Yehonatan?"

**9:2** And-to-[the]-house of-Sha'ul [there was] a-servant, and-his-name [was] Tsiva, and-they-called him to David. And-said to-him the-king, "Are-you Tsiva?" And-he-said, "Your-servant [is he]."

**9:3** And-said the-king, "Is-there-not yet a-man to-[the]-house of-Sha'ul, and-I-will-do with-him [the]-covenant-faithfulness [chesed] of-God [Elohim]?" And-said Tsiva to the-king, "Yet [there is] a-son to-Yehonatan, stricken of-feet [nekeh raglayim]."

**9:4** And-said to-him the-king, "Where [is]-he?" And-said Tsiva to the-king, "Behold-him [in the]-house of-Makhir son of-Ammi'el, in-Lo-Devar."

**9:5** And-sent the-king David, and-took-him from-[the]-house of-Makhir son of-Ammi'el, from-Lo-Devar.

**9:6** And-came Mefivoshet son of-Yehonatan son of-Sha'ul to David, and-fell upon his-face and-bowed-down. And-said David, "Mefivoshet!" And-he-said, "Behold your-servant."

**9:7** And-said to-him David, "Do-not fear, for doing I-will-do with-you covenant-faithfulness [chesed] for-the-sake-of Yehonatan your-father, and-I-will-restore to-you all [the]-field of-Sha'ul your-grandfather [literally: father], and-you will-eat bread [lechem] at-my-table continually [tamid]."

**9:8** And-he-bowed-down and-said, "What [is] your-servant, that you-have-turned to the-dead dog [ha-kelev ha-met] that [is] like-me?"

**9:9** And-called the-king to Tsiva, servant of-Sha'ul, and-said to-him, "All that was to-Sha'ul and-to-all his-house I-have-given to-[the]-son of-your-lord.

**9:10** And-you-shall-work for-him the-land, you and-your-sons and-your-servants, and-you-shall-bring-in, and-it-shall-be to-[the]-son of-your-lord bread [lechem] and-he-shall-eat. And-Mefivoshet son of-your-lord shall-eat continually [tamid] bread at-my-table." And-to-Tsiva [were] fifteen sons and-twenty servants.

**9:11** And-said Tsiva to the-king, "According-to-all that my-lord the-king commands his-servant, so shall-do your-servant." "And-Mefivoshet [shall be]-eating at-my-table as-one of-[the]-sons of-the-king."

**9:12** And-to-Mefivoshet [was] a-young son, and-his-name [was] Mikha. And-all [the]-dwelling of-[the]-house of-Tsiva [were]-servants to-Mefivoshet.

**9:13** And-Mefivoshet [was]-dwelling in-Yerushalayim, for at-[the]-table of-the-king continually [tamid] he [was]-eating. And-he [was]-lame [pisseach] in-both his-feet.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — chesed:** The chapter is structured around David's desire to show *chesed* — covenant-faithfulness — to the house of Saul. This is not mere kindness but the fulfillment of the covenant sworn with Jonathan (1 Sam 20:14-17). The word appears in vv.1, 3, and 7.

**v.3 — nekeh raglayim:** Literally "stricken of feet." This euphemism for lameness avoids specifying the exact nature of the disability. The backstory is given in 2 Sam 4:4 — Mephibosheth was dropped by his nurse as a five-year-old when fleeing after the battle of Gilboa.

**v.4 — Lo-Devar:** The place name לֹא דְבָר can be read as "no-thing" or "no-pasture" — a desolate place. Some scholars see a wordplay: the forgotten heir of Saul's house lives in "Nothing-town."

**v.8 — ha-kelev ha-met:** "The dead dog" is an expression of extreme self-abasement. A living dog was already contemptible (cf. 1 Sam 24:14); a dead dog is utterly worthless. Mephibosheth uses this of himself, reflecting his position as a disabled survivor of a fallen dynasty.

**v.11 — textual note:** The MT is awkward here. The phrase "And Mephibosheth shall eat at my table" appears to be David's speech inserted into the narrator's report of Ziba's reply. Some scholars regard it as a scribal gloss reinforcing the key motif.

*— EMET*
